name: CertiQR – Certificate Generator & QR Verification
author: attestra

sections.description:
CertiQR turns your WordPress site into the place where your certificates, licences and compliance documents are issued and checked. Every credential gets a unique ID and a QR code. Anyone holding a certificate — an employer, a client, an auditor — scans the code or types the ID into your verification page and sees straight away whether it is genuine.

Every check runs four tests and reports each one separately:

  1. The record exists in your register.
  2. Its issuer signature matches, so a record altered outside the plugin shows up as altered.
  3. It has not been withdrawn.
  4. It falls inside its validity window.

Generate certificates from your own artwork

Upload a JPG or PNG background, then place the holder’s name, course, dates, credential ID and QR code on it in the visual template editor. Every credential issued in that category gets its certificate automatically.

Features

  • Unlimited credentials, categories, templates and custom fields
  • Categories with their own ID pattern, validity period and fields
  • Text, long text and date fields, each with its own control over whether it is required, shown publicly, and available to the certificate
  • Visual template editor with three bundled open-licence fonts
  • Verification page with QR scanning and pretty URLs
  • Automatic expiry, withdrawal with a public reason, reinstatement, and a full amendment history
  • Issue emails with the certificate attached as a PDF
  • CSV export of the whole register or one category
  • Full backup (direct download) and restore of credentials, categories, templates and settings
  • [certiqr_verify], [certiqr_record] and [certiqr_count] shortcodes
  • Matches your site’s colours automatically, including Elementor global colours
  • Works with any theme and page builder

CertiQR Pro

Everything above is free with no limits on how many credentials you issue. CertiQR Pro is a separate add-on for organisations that need more. It adds:

  • QR codes on documents you already have — inspection reports, signed licences, multi-page PDFs — and PDF template backgrounds
  • CSV import, batches, and bulk upload of existing documents
  • Sequential numbering, and changing an ID after issue
  • Verification by uploading a certificate or a photo of one, a surname check, and a verification log with charts
  • Download buttons for holders, admin downloads in PDF, JPEG and PNG, and certificate protection
  • Choice of what the verification page shows, a public register, and nine more field types
  • Custom email wording per category, renewal reminders, white-label branding, four more fonts, bulk rebuilding and scheduled reports
  • Updates and support from the people who wrote the plugin

A 7-day trial is available from our website.

Credits

Bundled fonts (Great Vibes, Lato, Playfair Display) are used under the SIL Open Font License; the licence texts are in assets/fonts.
sections.installation:
1. Install CertiQR from Plugins → Add New, or upload the zip under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate it.
  3. CertiQR asks for a verification page. Choose a page you have already built, or let it create one for you.
  4. Create a category (CertiQR → Categories), attach a template if you want generated certificates, and issue your first credential.

CertiQR → Help includes a readiness check for your server and step-by-step guides.
sections.faq:
Is there a limit on how many credentials I can issue?

No. The free plugin has no limits on credentials, categories, templates or fields.

Does CertiQR send any data to you or anyone else?

No. Credentials, certificates and verification lookups stay on your own site. The plugin makes no outside requests.

Can people verify without an account?

Yes. Verification is public, needs no login, and always reflects the credential’s current status — so a withdrawn or expired credential says so.

What happens to issued QR codes if I change my verification page?

Every QR code points at your verification page’s address. Choose the page before you issue in earnest, and keep it at the same address afterwards; if you renumber a credential, its old ID keeps resolving.

Which image formats can a template background use?

JPG, PNG, WebP and GIF. PDF backgrounds are part of CertiQR Pro.

Do I need CertiQR Pro?

Only if you need the features listed under CertiQR Pro above, such as putting QR codes on documents you already have or issuing many credentials at once. CertiQR Pro is a separate plugin that works alongside this one; your data carries straight across.
sections.changelog:
3.45.4

  • Fixed: Plugin URI now points to the site homepage instead of /features, so WordPress.org’s URL check no longer depends on a heavy Elementor page regenerating on a cold cache.

3.45.3

  • Inline brand, button and font CSS is now validated and escaped at output.

3.45.2

  • Upgrading from the original Attestra plugin: activating CertiQR switches the old plugin off and takes over its credentials, settings, verification page and licence – no migration needed. Deleting the old plugin afterwards keeps your data.

3.45.1

  • Renamed to CertiQR. Existing data, settings and the old [attestra_*] shortcodes keep working.
  • Backups are now downloaded straight to your computer and are never stored on the server.
  • Restoring a backup reads the uploaded file directly and only restores certificate images and PDFs.
  • All admin styles and scripts are now loaded through the WordPress enqueue system.
  • Additional nonce and input checks on every admin form.

3.45.0

  • First release in the WordPress.org directory.
  • Dates written day-first in any form — 18/10/2026, 18-10-2026, 2026-10-18 or a written date — are read correctly, and a date that cannot be read is refused with a clear message instead of being stored as 1 January 1970.
  • Bulk tools, document uploads, PDF backgrounds, verification by upload and logging, downloads, reminders, branding and other advanced features live in the separate CertiQR Pro add-on.
